title: Canonical composition comparison for unbounded ringed-topos direct images
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be sites small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], carrying sheaves of commutative rings $A,B,C$, respectively. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)$ and $g:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),C)$ be morphisms of ringed topoi: their underlying functors are adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, the inverse images preserve finite limits, and the structural ring maps are $f^{-1}B\to A$ and $g^{-1}C\to B$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], direct image has underlying abelian direct image with the target-ring action induced by these structural maps. Write $D(A),D(B),D(C)$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $Rf_*,Rg_*,R(gf)_*$ for the total right derived direct images computed with K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Let $Q$ denote localization of cochain complexes of $A$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\kappa_{g,f}:R(g\circ f)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*.$$
Its normalization is as follows: for a K-injective complex $I$ of $A$-modules and a K-injective resolution $j:f_*I\to J$ of $B$-module complexes, the map $g_*f_*I\xrightarrow{g_*j}g_*J$ is a quasi-isomorphism and its class is $\kappa_{g,f,QI}$ under the canonical resolution identifications. These identifications and the comparison are natural in the derived argument.
